name: Sonja Koch
role: Federal Judge, Second Criminal Law Division, Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland (Bundesrichterin; juge fédérale à la deuxième Cour de droit pénal)
party: Schweizerische Volkspartei (SVP), as published by the Federal Supreme Court
bio: Sonja Koch, born in 1976, is a judge of the Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland and, as of October 2026, sits in its Second Criminal Law Division. She was elected a federal judge by the United Federal Assembly on 25 September 2019, on a party's proposal, as Swiss federal judges are; the Court lists her party as the SVP (Swiss People's Party). A lawyer admitted to the Aargau bar in 2004 with a doctorate obtained in 2014, she worked as a court clerk at the Lenzburg District Court and the Federal Supreme Court, as a scientific officer at the Federal Office of Justice and, from 2014 to 2019, as a presiding judge (Gerichtspräsidentin) at the Bernese Jura-Seeland Regional Court, before serving as a deputy judge of the Federal Supreme Court in 2018–2019. In September 2023 she presided over the panel in cases 7B_15/2021 and 7B_16/2021, whose statement that a lower court could take into account the relatively short duration of a rape in sentencing was disavowed by the Court in a separate 2024 judgment; the collegial judgment does not identify the author of that passage or how each judge voted.
